title: y = mx + b: a line as a rule

slides.title: A rule for the whole wire
slides.text: Tally wants to know how high a wire is at any step across, without drawing it. The wire starts at height 2 and climbs 1 for every 2 steps. A short rule can give its height at step 6, and at step 600 just as easily.

slides.title: Start, then a steady change
slides.text: The rule is y = 0.5x + 2. The number added, 2, is the height at x = 0, called the y-intercept. The number that multiplies x, 0.5, is the slope: the change in y for each step of x. In y = mx + b, the slope is m and the y-intercept is b.

visual.label: The line y = 0.5x + 2 with its start and its slope

focus.cue: The line starts at 2 on the y-axis: b = 2.
It rises 2 while it runs 4, so m = 2/4 = 0.5.

slides.title: Build a rule from two points
slides.text: A line passes through (1, 3) and (3, 7). Find the slope first. Then step back from one point to x = 0 to find where the line starts, and check the rule with the other point.

slides.title: One output for each input
slides.text: A function is a rule that gives exactly one output for each input. A table shows it as pairs, and a graph shows the same pairs as points. A story can hold a function too: a tank with 20 liters that loses 2 liters each minute holds y = 20 − 2x liters after x minutes.

slides.title: Not every rule is a line
slides.text: A linear function changes by the same amount for each step, so its graph is straight. The outputs 0, 1, 4, 9 of y = x² change by 1, then 3, then 5. Their points bend into a curve, so that function is not linear.

visual.label: Four points of y = x² that do not lie on one line

focus.cue: From x = 0 to x = 1 the output goes up 1.
From x = 2 to x = 3 it goes up 5: the steps change.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.text: Four words for lines as rules.

words.means: a rule that gives exactly one output for each input
a function whose graph is a straight line, such as y = 2x + 1
the value of y where a line crosses the y-axis, at x = 0
how much y changes for each step of 1 in x: the slope

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Sky Lines at Wire Rules. Give each wire its start height and its steepness, from a table, a story or two islands. Then find the table that bends.
slides.alt: Sky Lines on a phone: a grid with a wire's start marked at height 2, and a stepper to set its height at 6 across.
